report_name: AI 'Slopsquatting' Emerges as New Software Supply Chain Threat

attack_patterns.name: Compromise Software Dependencies and Development Tools
attack_patterns.description: Threat actors perform slopsquatting by registering plausible but fake package names hallucinated by AI assistants and uploading malicious code, compromising the software supply chain when developers install these dependencies.

attack_patterns.name: JavaScript
attack_patterns.description: Malicious code within slopsquatted npm packages is executed via JavaScript when installed or used by a developer.

attack_patterns.name: Python
attack_patterns.description: Malicious code within slopsquatted PyPI packages is executed via Python when installed or used by a developer.

attack_patterns.name: Discover LLM Hallucinations
attack_patterns.description: Threat actors study the patterns of AI coding assistants to discover which plausible-sounding but non-existent package names are frequently 'hallucinated'.

attack_patterns.name: Publish Hallucinated Entities
attack_patterns.description: Threat actors proactively register the hallucinated package names discovered from AI assistants in public repositories like npm and PyPI, uploading malicious software to these names.

tools.name: GitHub Copilot
tools.description: An AI coding assistant whose tendency to 'hallucinate' non-existent software package names is exploited as the basis for slopsquatting attacks.

tools.name: ChatGPT
tools.description: An AI assistant whose tendency to 'hallucinate' non-existent software package names is exploited as the basis for slopsquatting attacks.

tools.name: npm
tools.description: A package manager for JavaScript used by developers, which can be tricked into installing malicious 'slopsquatted' packages from the npm registry.

tools.name: pip
tools.description: A package manager for Python used by developers, which can be tricked into installing malicious 'slopsquatted' packages from the PyPI repository.

campaigns.name: Slopsquatting
campaigns.description: A software supply chain attack vector that exploits AI coding assistants' tendency to hallucinate non-existent package names, which are then registered by threat actors with malicious code.
campaigns.objective: Compromise developer environments and inject malicious code into the software supply chain.

identities.name: Developers
identities.description: Developers who use AI coding assistants and are targeted by slopsquatting attacks when they inadvertently install malicious packages suggested by the AI.

infrastructure.name: Malicious Package Repositories
infrastructure.description: Public package repositories like npm and PyPI where threat actors upload malicious packages under hallucinated names to perform slopsquatting attacks.

indicators.name: Installation of Hallucinated Python Package python-http
indicators.pattern:
title: Potential Slopsquatting via Common AI Hallucinated Package Installation
id: 9c5b1a3d-8f6e-4b2c-9d1a-5e7f6a3b2c1d
status: experimental
description: Detects the installation of the 'python-http' package, a common AI hallucination that does not exist as a legitimate package and is a candidate for slopsquatting.
references:
  - https://thehackernews.com/2026/07/weekly-recap-rogue-ai-agents-check.html
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-07-27
tags:
  - attack.t1195.001
  - attack.initial_access
falsepositives:
  - Unlikely, as 'python-http' is not a standard or known legitimate package. The correct package is 'requests'.
level: medium
logsource:
  category: process_creation
detection:
  selection:
    CommandLine|contains: 'pip install python-http'
  condition: selection
indicators.description: Detects the installation of 'python-http', a non-existent package commonly hallucinated by AI assistants, indicating a potential slopsquatting attack.
